title: Join strings with a Buffer
hints: The starter already copies every part into the buffer. What's missing is the separator between them.
The separator goes before every part except the first. `List.iteri` hands your function the index as well as the part.
`List.iteri (fun i p -> if i > 0 then Buffer.add_string b sep; Buffer.add_string b p) parts`.
explain: The reference uses `List.iteri` and adds `sep` before every part whose index is above 0, then returns `Buffer.contents b`. An empty list gives the empty string, one part gives the part itself, and the separator never appears at either end.
